gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Brushed lines of constant width, with lowercase heavy as poured lead: that's Origami up top. And Noto Sans Elymaic follows with open apertures and ascenders barely clearing the x-height, so paragraphs run low and unhurried.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-inscript: Origami makes round letters with no stress tilt at all. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian brings big open eyes and a deep middle band, so it rewards a slightly larger size than usual.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Origami: single-stroke brush lettering, heavy as poured lead. Noto Sans Kaithi fills its lines with lowercase that stands nearly like capitals, so the heading's gentle monotone line and the body's open e sit comfortably together.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Zero stroke contrast, all brush: Origami lays down lowercase like cast lead. Noto Sans Lepcha lets its curves stay generously open beneath lowercase with cast iron stature, and that shared heft is the link.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-malayala: Pure sign-painter brushwork: Origami keeps one constant stroke, no mid-curve swelling, and lowercase like poured lead. Origami grabs attention; Noto Sans Malayalam builds texture with its dominant middle zone.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Origami's brush strokes never swell or slow the eye. Noto Sans Mandaic lifts lowercase close to capital height and keeps curvy letters loose, a lively foil that is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-nabataea: Noto Sans Nabataean reads tall and open, its lowercase standing almost cap-high with generous s curves. And Origami meets it with one neon-tube track width, so the heading feels drawn and the text feels set.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-nag-mund: Origami's monoline strokes look pulled straight from a brush. Noto Sans Nag Mundari counters with half-unwrapped curves and lowercase that rivals capitals, and both standing tall is the draw.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-old-hung: Noto Sans Old Hungarian opens up every tall a, e and s. Origami's unmodulated line makes the best contrast, a brushy mass over apertures that stay open at tiny sizes.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-old-ital: Origami bends its strokes like copper pipe. Noto Sans Old Italic keeps lowercase nearly cap-tall with curve endings well apart, so the tubular heading and the tidy text feel cut from one idea.
